items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Ben Borders was the drummer and leader

ctx.x: I've seen the sign. The hotel is still there.

Right. Well, I guess it's still there. And it was an old hotel then. You know, it had been a very prominent hotel at that time. I don't say it was as prominent as the Biltmore, but I guess you would call it about a second or third rate hotel, and it had music, and I was working with a little group. Ben Borders was the drummer and leader, and then Jim Wynn, who became very well known, and who passed on about a year and a half ago, a saxophone player. And there was another -- let me see, there was a trumpet player,…

Theater, he was a doorman there and doing other little jobs around. So we had decided that I was going to work about two more weeks and then take off and get ready for the baby, you know. And we were both anxiously awaiting this baby. And lo and behold, one day I went shopping and my sister Florida who was living with my husband and I at that time, she hadn't been in California but about six months, but anyway, she went shopping with me and we were shopping for the baby, you know.
